featured_reviews.name: SGT Reviews
featured_reviews.review_text:
Brijwasi Sweets – Prabhadevi | A mixed bag, literally

We visited the Prabhadevi outlet with a simple plan: pick up 2.5–3 kilos of assorted sweets and be done in one smooth stop.

Taste-wise?
No complaints. Brijwasi does what Brijwasi does best the sweets were fresh, well-made, and true to their flavour. You know the brand, you know the taste, and that part still holds strong.

But here’s where the experience slipped.

Availability was a real letdown.
For a brand this established and a branch in a prime area like Prabhadevi, the spread was surprisingly limited. Several items weren’t available in the quantity we needed, which made putting together a proper mixed order unnecessarily difficult.

So while the quality didn’t disappoint, the choice definitely did.

Final word:
If you’re going in for a specific sweet and small quantities, you’ll likely walk out happy.
But if you’re planning a bulk purchase or a wide assortment, be prepared availability might not match expectations.

Taste ✅
Brand trust ✅
Variety ❌
Bulk buying experience ❌

Sometimes, the sweetness is there… just not enough of it.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Panshikar had been on my list for its reputation for Maharashtrian snacks, and I finally visited yesterday evening. Conveniently located just outside Dadar railway station, I was eager to try their specialties.
I started with the Misal Pav, which wasn't quite my style due to the farsan, poha, and batatyachi bhaji making it a bit soggy. However, the taste was decent, though slightly on the sweeter side.
Next, I tried the Bhajani Thalipeet it was deep-fried and tasted good, paired with their lasun chutney, which was absolutely delicious.
The star of the evening, however, was the Kothimbir Vadi. It was perfectly cooked—crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, making it an absolute treat.
I ended the meal with Piyush which is a must-try and a great way to conclude the meal.
Overall, the experience was good. The service was fast and efficient, and I appreciated the quick turnaround. A heads-up: Panshikar is closed on Sundays.
If you're in the mood for some classic Maharashtrian snacks, this is definitely worth a visit!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Modakam Restaurant ,Near Siddhivinayak Temple
Modakam restaurant, located just beside Siddhivinayak Mandir, is a great place to visit after darshan. I honestly didn’t expect such authentic and fresh food.
They serve freshly made Ukdiche Modak, which is a must-try. The restaurant offers a good variety of Maharashtrian and North Indian dishes.
I tried Puran Poli, Tea, and Pav Bhaji everything tasted amazing and fresh. The flavors were authentic and satisfying.
The service was good and staff were polite. However, you may have to wait around 15–20 minutes for seating, especially during peak hours, but it’s definitely worth the wait.
Overall, it’s a must-visit place near Siddhivinayak Temple if you want to enjoy good food after darshan.

featured_reviews.name: Mayur Suvarna
featured_reviews.review_text: Tried food at this place during visit to siddhivinayak temple. It's the only restaurant which is available very nearby and inside the temple premises. If you have a family and senior citizen who cannot walk much, it's the go through place due to its locality. We had their Punjabi Thali, happy to see that because it was as same as displayed on the hotel walls as a covershot. Because very few restaurants serves food as displayed on the menu. The thali looked beautiful and delicious as well, looking at my thali the new customers who sat beside me also enquired me with which is the dish and also ordered the same. Also we tried their modam which was piping hot drizzled with ghee. Even if the place is compact and small but it's clean and hygiene maintained is very well, service is fast and well managed to maintain the flow of crowd due to small place even with the place constraint the menu range is wide and long. We also tried their Panner Noodles, Chaas and Mango juice (Seasonal). Puran Poli's are also available here. During rush hours and busy day you need to wait for the table due to the limited space and place.

featured_reviews.review_text:

Their Modak Special Thali was super filling and full of flavors, it included 3 chapatis, 2 types of paneer bhaji, dahi vada, jeera rice, dal tadka, achar, papad, and a tasty modak with ghee on top.

The food quality and taste were definitely worth it, especially if you love authentic Maharashtrian food.

The only downside was the waiting time, which was quite long, but overall the experience and food made up for it.
